tasks.title: Class → struct
tasks.statement: Python: class Dog with name and a speak() method → «<name>: гав!». Write a struct Dog { name: String }, a function new(name: &str) -> Dog, and a method speak(&self) -> String.
tasks.hint: format!("{}: гав!", self.name)

tasks.title: property
tasks.statement: Python: @property celsius / fahrenheit. A struct Temp { celsius: f64 } with a method fahrenheit(&self) -> f64 (c · 9/5 + 32) and set_fahrenheit(&mut self, f: f64) (updates celsius).
tasks.hint: Formulas: c·9/5+32 and (f−32)·5/9.

tasks.title: classmethod
tasks.statement: Python: Color.from_hex("#ff8000"). A struct Color { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 } and an associated function from_hex(s: &str) -> Color for a string of the form «#rrggbb» (use u8::from_str_radix(&s[1..3], 16).unwrap()).
tasks.hint: u8::from_str_radix(&s[1..3], 16).unwrap()

tasks.title: Composition instead of inheritance
tasks.statement: Python: class Employee(Person). Structs Person { name: String } and Employee { person: Person, salary: u32 }; Employee has a method describe(&self) -> String: «<name> зарабатывает <salary>».
tasks.hint: self.person.name is a field of the nested struct.

tasks.title: First trait
tasks.statement: A trait Animal with a method sound(&self) -> String; structs Dog and Cat implement it: «гав» and «мяу». The function chorus(a: &impl Animal) -> String returns the sound repeated three times separated by spaces.
tasks.hint: impl Animal for Dog { … } — a separate block for each type.

tasks.title: Default method
tasks.statement: A trait Greeter: the method name(&self) -> String is required, and greet(&self) -> String has a default implementation: «Привет, <name>!». The struct English implements only name; the struct Formal overrides greet: «Здравствуйте, <name>.».
tasks.hint: The default method calls the required one: self.name().

tasks.title: Vector of shapes
tasks.statement: A trait Shape with area(&self) -> f64; structs Circle { r } and Rect { w, h } implement it (π ≈ 3.14159). The function total_area(shapes: &[Box<dyn Shape>]) -> f64 is the sum of the areas.
tasks.hint: shapes.iter().map(|s| s.area()).sum()

tasks.title: Display for a point
tasks.statement: Implement fmt::Display for the struct Point { x: i32, y: i32 }: output «(x, y)». Then println!("{}", p) and p.to_string() will give «(1, -2)».
tasks.hint: write!(f, "({}, {})", self.x, self.y)

tasks.title: Debug and PartialEq
tasks.statement: Add the derive(Debug, PartialEq, Clone) attributes to the struct Pair { a: i32, b: i32 } so that {:?} printing, == comparison, and clone() work.
tasks.hint: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Clone)] above the struct.

tasks.title: Version order
tasks.statement: The struct Version(u32, u32, u32) with derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug): versions are compared lexicographically. Complete the function newest(v: &[Version]) -> Version, returning the greatest (v is non-empty; Version also needs Clone and Copy).
tasks.hint: derive(Ord) compares fields in order; iter().max().

tasks.title: Adding vectors
tasks.statement: For Vec2 { x: f64, y: f64 } implement the + and − operators (the traits Add and Sub). Derive(Debug, PartialEq, Clone, Copy) is already there.
tasks.hint: Add component by component.

tasks.title: Multiplying by a number
tasks.statement: For Vec2 implement Mul<f64> (vector × number) and Neg (unary minus).
tasks.hint: impl Mul<f64> for Vec2 — the right operand type goes in angle brackets.

tasks.title: Dot product
tasks.statement: For Vec2 implement Mul<Vec2> with Output = f64 (the dot product): a * b = a.x·b.x + a.y·b.y.
tasks.hint: Output can be a different type from the operands themselves.

tasks.statement: For Money(i64) (kopecks) implement Add and AddAssign so that a + b and a += b work. Derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq) is already there.
tasks.hint: add_assign takes &mut self and returns nothing.

tasks.title: Matrix indexing
tasks.statement: A struct Matrix { w: usize, data: Vec<i32> } (row by row). Implement Index<(usize, usize)> and IndexMut<(usize, usize)> so that m[(r, c)] works for reading and writing.
tasks.hint: &self.data[r * self.w + c] and &mut …

tasks.title: Fraction
tasks.statement: A struct Frac { n: i64, d: i64 } with a function new(n, d) -> Frac that reduces the fraction by the GCD and keeps the denominator positive, with the operators Add and Mul, and Display «n/d» (when d = 1 — just «n»).
tasks.hint: First reduce by the GCD, then normalize the sign of the denominator.

tasks.title: Custom iterator
tasks.statement: The struct Countdown { n: u32 } implements Iterator<Item = u32>: next() yields n, n−1, …, 1, then None.
tasks.hint: The state is stored in self; when n == 0 — None. The other iterator methods come for free.

tasks.title: Fibonacci iterator
tasks.statement: The struct Fib { a: u64, b: u64 } implements Iterator<Item = u64>: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, … (infinite). Add a function fib() -> Fib that returns the initial state.
tasks.hint: An infinite iterator always returns Some; take limits it.

tasks.title: Drop
tasks.statement: The struct Noisy { name: String } prints «drop <name>» when destroyed. Implement Drop; the driver will show the output order.
tasks.hint: println!("drop {}", self.name)

tasks.title: Default
tasks.statement: The struct Settings { volume: u8, name: String, muted: bool } with derive(Debug, Default). Add the derive and write a function quiet() -> Settings: default values, but muted = true (via ..Default::default()).
tasks.hint: #[derive(Debug, Default)] and ..Default::default().

tasks.title: Chained builder
tasks.statement: A struct Pizza { size: u32, cheese: bool, toppings: Vec<String> }. Write Pizza::new(size), the methods with_cheese(mut self) -> Pizza and with_topping(mut self, t: &str) -> Pizza, and describe(&self) -> String of the form «30 см, сыр, начинки: гриб, лук» (without cheese — no «сыр»; without toppings — no «начинки»).
tasks.hint: Builder methods take self by value and return it.

tasks.title: Newtype: vector wrapper
tasks.statement: Implement fmt::Display for the wrapper struct Wrapper(Vec<String>): output «[a, b, c]» (elements separated by a comma and a space).
tasks.hint: self.0 is the vector inside the wrapper.

tasks.title: Stack as a struct
tasks.statement: A struct Stack { items: Vec<i32> } with the methods new(), push(&mut self, x), pop(&mut self) -> Option<i32>, peek(&self) -> Option<i32>, len(&self) -> usize, and is_empty(&self) -> bool.
tasks.hint: The methods delegate to the vector inside.

tasks.title: Queue on two stacks
tasks.statement: Implement a queue Queue { inbox: Vec<i32>, outbox: Vec<i32> } with push(x), pop() -> Option<i32> (FIFO), and len(). When outbox is empty, move all elements of inbox into it in reverse order.
tasks.hint: Moving from inbox to outbox reverses the order.

tasks.title: Plugins
tasks.statement: A trait Plugin { fn name(&self) -> String; fn run(&self, x: i32) -> i32; }. The structs Doubler and AddN { n: i32 } implement it (names «doubler» and «add»). The function pipeline(ps: &[Box<dyn Plugin>], x: i32) -> i32 applies the plugins in sequence.
tasks.hint: Loop over &[Box<dyn Plugin>] and call p.run(v).

tasks.title: Generic function with a trait
tasks.statement: Write a function largest<T: PartialOrd + Copy>(v: &[T]) -> T that returns the greatest element of a slice (non-empty). It must work for i32, f64, and char alike.
tasks.hint: The bound T: PartialOrd + Copy lets you compare and copy.

tasks.title: From for conversions
tasks.statement: The structs Celsius(f64) and Fahrenheit(f64). Implement From<Celsius> for Fahrenheit (c · 9/5 + 32); then Fahrenheit::from(c) and c.into() work.

tasks.title: Custom equality
tasks.statement: The struct Name(String): two names are equal ignoring case. Implement PartialEq by hand (the eq method).
tasks.hint: Compare the lowercase versions of the strings.

tasks.title: Custom ordering
tasks.statement: The struct Prio(u32): the order is reversed — the larger number is “smaller” (comes first). Implement PartialOrd by hand (partial_cmp). PartialEq is derived.
tasks.hint: Swap the operands: other.0.partial_cmp(&self.0).

tasks.title: Trait with a static function
tasks.statement: A trait Zero { fn zero() -> Self; }. Implement it for i32 and f64. The function sum_all<T: Zero + std::ops::Add<Output = T> + Copy>(v: &[T]) -> T adds up the elements, starting from T::zero().
tasks.hint: T::zero() is called through the type parameter name.
